page.layout: One text page with two blocks. The running text runs full width from the top. Below it, the two-column Arabic word list is set in parallel columns: left column with the transliteration and gloss pairs, right column with the same. Then continued running text at full width below. No margin notes, no running head, no catchword.

main_text.l: 3. Articulare est articuli ال ὁ ἡ τὸ [?],
quo pertinet relativum الذي [?] alladi, cum
In hisce omnibus initiale privatur vocali
sua, nisi sententiam inchoat, aut initio
assumit literas servile: quo casu Elif sæpè
exci-dit, ut [?] pro [?], & perpetuum est in
particula ال quoties Lam servile præfigitur, ut

page.notes: Arabic words are set in Arabic letters, but several glyphs are uncertain and are marked [?]: the Arabic before "congregatus est", the Arabic of each list entry, the Arabic forms in the "ut ... pro ..." example, the article and relative pronoun, and the Greek article forms (τὸ marked as read). The "ut" at the end of the page is the last printed line of the running text, not a catchword. The vertical bar after "omnibus" in the line "In hisce omnibus | initiale" is a printed mark and is left out. Printed "eft" is transcribed as "est", "fcil." as "scil.", and "fervile"/"praefigitur" with long s as plain s. The "IO." in "in IO. nominibus" is copied as printed.
